note: Every ruling here is PROVISIONAL and owned by someone at Thornbury, not by us. See docs/working-answers.md for the reasoning, the cost of being wrong, and who overturns each one. This file is hand-authored and reviewed; it is NOT derived. reference/spec-7.json and reference/supplier-master.json ARE derived - do not hand-edit those.

spec_staleness.why: SPEC-7 has an annual review cycle and rev D took effect 2026-03-01. Nobody owns telling this repo that a revision issued, so it assumes its copy goes stale on schedule and says so loudly rather than asserting a withdrawn rule in silence.

unit_conversions.why: SPEC-7 s2 requires a result in a different unit to be converted before comparison, and the conversion recorded. COA-0027 and COA-0031 report ppb against a ppm limit.
mg/kg and ppm are the same quantity for solids. Not present in the sample; included because it is the most likely next variant and the conversion is exact.

attribute_synonyms.why: Treat these as naming the same attribute. Never merge across METHOD - method is carried separately and is part of whether a result counts at all (SPEC-7 s3.1).

ladder: 1. unambiguous by construction - ISO 8601, a written month, or a slash date with a component > 12
2. the document states its own convention in prose - reading a document's own instructions is not inference
date_resolution.why_no_supplier_inference: An earlier version (ADR-0006) added a rung that resolved an ambiguous date from >=3 agreeing certificates by the same supplier. Dropped: we already refuse to infer Zeeland Bulk BV's convention because indirect evidence is not safe enough to release a lot on, and inferring Halewood's is the same class of move with marginally more evidence. The line between them was a threshold we chose, and it had been calibrated on the single case it admitted. Consistency is worth more than the one document it recovered.

evidence_considered_but_not_acted_on.note: Kept because it is real analysis and the next team should not have to redo it. It is NOT read by any code.
evidence_considered_but_not_acted_on.Zeeland Bulk BV: no unambiguous slash date anywhere in the corpus - nothing to infer from

rules.message: Supplier is not on the approved supplier master. The ERP will not create a lot for it. Either the master is out of date or this material is from an unapproved source - both need someone to look.
The certificate states two different lot numbers. We will not choose between them - which one is right determines which physical material this is.
A result is outside the SPEC-7 acceptance limits. SPEC-7 s5: non-conforming irrespective of any conformance statement on the certificate.
The certificate states conformance for a result that is outside the limits. SPEC-7 s5: the certificate is in error and the lot is referred to Quality. The supplier needs correcting too.
The certificate cites a withdrawn revision of SPEC-7. SPEC-7 s4: the lot is referred to Quality and shall not be accepted on the strength of the certificate alone.
An attribute was determined by a method that is not reportable for it under SPEC-7 s2. SPEC-7 s3.1: the result is indicative and cannot be used to determine acceptance. s4: refer to Quality.
The certificate does not report every attribute SPEC-7 s2 requires. A missing attribute is not a passing one.
A date on this certificate reads two ways and no convention resolves it. Nothing is wrong with the lot - we could not read the document.

The certificate states no retest date, and the ERP requires an expiry date. Every certificate that carries both sets retest at manufacture + 24 months, so this COULD be calculated - we will not, because that date drives Purchasing's reorder logic and inventing it is not ours to do.

A required field could not be read from this document. Nothing is wrong with the lot - this layout is one the parser does not recognise. It goes back to manual keying, as all volume does today. This rule leads all others (order 5): if the document did not parse, every other finding on it is drawn from fields we may have misread.

erp_mapping.status: PRESERVES CURRENT PRACTICE - not a recommendation
erp_mapping.why: The intake team already keys the certificate's retest date into the ERP's expiry_date. They are not the same thing and Denis has said so. We preserve today's behaviour rather than silently changing what Purchasing reorders against; our own output keeps retest_date under its own name so the two are never conflated in OUR record.
erp_mapping.cannot_note: See docs/open-questions.md C1-C4. The ERP holds less than the certificate states and less than QA records. That is a data-model gap in the ERP, not a mapping we can close.

release.why: The ERP already defaults status to held and releasing is a separate action. The system does not need the ability to release, so it does not have it. A person releases, exactly as today.

not_decided.what: The confidence threshold for accept vs hold
not_decided.why: It encodes Thornbury's tolerance for a recall against its tolerance for delay. Every hold this system issues today is mandated by a SPEC-7 rule above, not chosen by us, so no threshold is in force. One becomes necessary only if a non-deterministic extractor is added.

not_decided.what: Whether a manufacture date in the future should hold the lot
not_decided.why: Ten of 36 certificates carry one. A rule that sensible-sounding would hold 28% of the sample. Not adding it on our own judgement - see Q22.
